newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS-India PM vows new economic measures this week.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-India PM vows new economic measures this week.

text.p: Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Monday that new economic policy measures would be announced this week -- a clear message to investors in India to stop worrying about the government's commitment to reform.
"Some decisions will be coming in the next two to three days," Deve Gowda told the All India Association of Industries.

Investors in India's stock markets, anticipating good news was on the way, sent the Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark 30-share index 3.7 percent higher on Monday, gaining 127.12 points to finish at 3,562.74.

Share prices have risen around 15 percent since the beginning of the year, having plunged to a three-year low on December 4 as investors lost faith that Deve Gowda's multi-party coalition would follow through on promises of reform.
"My decisions will always be to give more opportunity and create a better investment climate for the investors," Deve Gowda said.
"With this background, forget the question of hesitation in the mind of the government while making decisions."
He said his seven-month-old goverment would stick by the policy of economic liberalisation mapped out by the former Congress Party government's finance minister Manmohan Singh.
"We will not deviate from the policies laid down by Manmohan Singh, the previous government. There is no need for a change in the policies. We have accepted them."
Deve Gowda said speculators were to blame for market volatility rather than the government's decision-making abilities.

"The decline in the capital markets or the fluctuation in the capital markets -- is it due to policy decisions of the government or due to players in the capital market. I would like the industrialists to tell me," Deve Gowda said.
"In seven months I cannot bring heaven to Earth. In a situation like this the government has to play its role and take a decision."
Despite the recent surge in share values, the markets have remained subject to wild swings, prompting worries that the bullish speculation was overheated.
The prime minister told the conference that new steps would be taken before he and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram went to Switzerland to attend the World Economic Forum in Davos on January 31.
Parliament's approval will be needed for further measures the government planned to announce in the budget set for February 28, he said.
Deve Gowda said policy decisions would be guided by the need to hit an annual investment target of $10 billion.
"It is not a question of favouring any individuals, but to get my target of 10 billion dollars a year, (that) I want to get from both domestic investors as well as global investors," he said.
"When I have this target in my mind, whatever decision are required, I will not hesitate to take them."
He also said said the government would approve all oustanding power projects within two months.
